title: Distributed Locking

searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: Martin Kleppmann: How to do distributed locking
sources.supportRationale: Original analysis of paused lease holders and resource-enforced fencing; not a blanket evaluation of every current Redis deployment.

sources.title: etcd v3.6: API guarantees
sources.supportRationale: Explicit v3.6 KV consistency, weaker serializable read option, watch limitations and lease behavior.

sources.title: Google SRE: Handling overload
sources.supportRationale: Capacity, bounded queues, load shedding and retry-aware overload reasoning.

sources.title: Amazon Builders’ Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter
sources.supportRationale: Timeout uncertainty, safe repeated effects, retry amplification, bounded retries and jitter; URL redirects to the author's AWS Builder Center article.

scenarios.theme: A worker pauses beyond its lease and overwrites a successor. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: Correctness requires obsolete owners not to mutate the shared document. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Distributed Locking to pause expiry.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A worker pauses beyond its lease and overwrites a successor. What changes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use a supported generation/conditional-mutation protocol enforced atomically by the document owner, and establish new authority before relying on obsolete-

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: The resource must cooperate and retain authority state

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A longer lease reduces frequency but is not a proof against an unbounded pause.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to fencing, etcd; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: An old unlock deletes a new owner’s lease. How do you fix it?
scenarios.assumptions: Worker A’s delayed release arrives after worker B acquired the same resource key. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Distributed Locking to safe release.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An old unlock deletes a new owner’s lease. How do you fix it?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Release only through an atomic owner-identity comparison in the supported lock service, scoped to A’s actual acquisition

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Identity metadata and atomic comparison are required

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A separate read then delete can race in the same way; owner-safe release still does not fence A’s old writes.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to fencing, etcd; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A renewal request times out. Continue the critical operation?
scenarios.assumptions: The holder cannot establish whether the lease remains valid and the mutation could corrupt authoritative state. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Distributed Locking to renewal unknown.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A renewal request times out. Continue the critical operation?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Stop starting unverified critical work, reconcile through the supported lease protocol, and make the resource enforce authority even for delayed in-flight

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Conservative stopping reduces availability

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Expendable duplicate refresh work can choose a weaker efficiency contract, but authoritative effects cannot silently use that assumption.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to etcd, fencing; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A third-party API ignores your fencing token. Is the lock enough?
scenarios.assumptions: A paused old holder can still call the provider after a new holder starts. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Distributed Locking to no fencing api.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A third-party API ignores your fencing token. Is the lock enough?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use provider-supported stable intent/idempotency/status semantics or move the invariant to a boundary that can enforce it

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A separate lock improves coordination but cannot force an unrelated API to reject old authority

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Manual reconciliation or a changed business promise may be necessary.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to fencing, retry; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.theme: Thousands of callers spin on one lock. What will you change?
scenarios.assumptions: Acquisition traffic overloads the coordinator and the protected operation takes seconds. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Distributed Locking to hot lock.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Thousands of callers spin on one lock. What will you change?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Bound contenders with deadlines/backoff and admission, shorten or remove the critical section where possible, and consider a queue or partitioned ownership

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Queueing adds latency and a queue itself needs a capacity/recovery contract

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: More coordinator replicas do not make one logically exclusive operation parallel.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to overload, etcd; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A restored resource forgets its highest accepted generation. What now?
scenarios.assumptions: Old delayed operations may still exist and a restored counter is lower than before the incident. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Distributed Locking to restore generation.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A restored resource forgets its highest accepted generation. What now?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Reestablish a non-regressing authority namespace/generation through the supported recovery procedure and exclude obsolete actors before accepting writes

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A safe reset may require downtime and coordinated fencing

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Increasing an in-memory number arbitrarily is not proof that all delayed old generations are excluded.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to fencing, etcd; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.
